_source: Transcribed from the GWMS Curriculum Guide in Notion, rebuilt September 26, 2026 for the three-games model. Game fields (games array) come from each session's Grappling Class Guide (Unit 7), Start 1 of each of the three CVP games, with the GWMS Game Rulings applied. TLO/ELO/connection/takeaway come from each session's Lesson and Intervention Guide. Nothing here is authored beyond plain-language rewording of the guides' own words.

stage.name: The Descent
stage.grapplingTlo: By the end of the Descent, participants will apply the Paths to move from a standing start through the guard into a controlled pin, using safe falling and the tap throughout.
stage.caselTlo: By the end of the Descent, participants will identify their own persona and shadow, naming the mask they perform, what cracks it under pressure, and one true thing underneath.
stage.connection: Getting past a partner's guard to what it protects is the same act as looking under a mask to the real person. The Descent digs deep, on the mat and inside you.

sessions.probingQuestion: What makes a place feel safe to you?

golmest.recapText: Orientation night. From now on: warm up, three games, lesson, this phone, cleanup.

standard.label: What you are here to learn

golmest.quizQuestion: What ends a round right away?
golmest.quizCorrect: Tapping your partner, tapping the mat, or saying stop.

sessions.connection: Tonight the room agreed on the rules together, out loud. That is what makes a place feel safe: everyone knows the rules will hold, and everyone had a hand in making them.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you learned the standing rules, the tap, and how to stop a round right away. Those rules work because everyone agreed to them out loud, together. You helped build them, not just follow them. A safe place is one you get to build, not just enter.

concept.lesson: The tap ends the round right away, and everyone agreed to it out loud.
concept.question: Tonight everyone agreed to the tap. What do you do the second your partner taps?

options.text: Let go and stop right away.
Finish the move first, then stop.
options.feedback: Finishing first is how people get hurt. Stop on the tap.

options.text: Wait for the coach to say stop.
options.feedback: The tap is enough. You stop without being told.

concept.bridge: Everyone stops on the tap, every time. That is what makes this place safe.

sessions.probingQuestion: How do you show up when nobody here knows you yet?

games.title: Over-Under to Close Hand Connection
games.start: Both players stand in an even tie, one arm over and one arm under, on both sides.
games.text: Fight to get under your partner's elbows. Connect your hands anywhere from his armpits to his ankles.

win.role: Whoever first locks his hands around his partner's body
win.text: wins, anywhere from armpits to ankles.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting to get an underhook.

games.title: Half Guard Side-Position Game
games.start: The bottom player is in half guard on his side, arms out straight. The top player is inside the half guard.
games.text: Top player: clear the bottom player's hands and get under at least one elbow, then connect your hands. Bottom player: keep your hands on the top player to deny that spot, and close your legs around his waist.

win.text: wins by locking his hands under the bottom player's elbow.
wins by closing his legs around the top player's waist.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting close while he blocks you.

games.title: Mount — Stay Under Both Elbows (Continuous)
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is in mount with both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
games.text: Top player: stay under at least one elbow the whole round. If you lose one, fight to get it back. Bottom player: get both elbows to touch your own body with nothing under them, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps an arm under one of the bottom player's elbows.
wins by getting both elbows to his body, or making the top player fall.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If he loses both elbows, that is the bottom player's win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is sitting on top of his belly.

sessions.connection: How you make first contact on the mat, careful, rushed, or stiff, is your entrance. Naming how you show up when nobody knows you yet is the same pattern, seen off the mat.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the over-under tie, half guard, and mount. How you make first contact on the mat, careful, rushed, or stiff, is your entrance. You can choose that entrance on purpose instead of by accident. Choosing how you show up works the same way off the mat.

concept.lesson: You make the connection on purpose, then you keep it instead of letting go.
concept.question: Tonight you connected to a stranger's wrist, legs, and elbow. What made it hold?

options.text: You made it on purpose, then you kept it.
You grabbed whatever was open and let it go.
options.feedback: Grabbing at random is not the same as making a connection.

options.text: You waited for him to make the first move.
options.feedback: Waiting is not how you make contact with a stranger.

concept.bridge: A connection made on purpose can hold. One grabbed at random can't.

sessions.probingQuestion: What are you like before you trust the room?

games.title: Hand Touch / Knee Touch Collection Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, no grips to start.
games.text: Hand fight and collect three touches, any mix. A touch is making your partner's hands touch the mat, or gripping behind one of his knees. Defend his touches at the same time.

win.text: wins the round. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is scoring touches while standing.

games.title: Belly-Up Open Guard Connection Foundation
games.start: The bottom player is belly up, feet in the middle, one hand on the top player's ankle. The top player is standing.
games.text: Bottom player: keep your feet hooked or posted on the top player at all times, and a hand on him too. Use that to put him on his hips or hands. Top player: break those connections with your hands and feet, and work to the outside for shin-to-body contact.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps a foot and a hand on the top player.
wins by getting free of the bottom player's feet and hands, going around his legs, and touching his body with a shin.

games.reset: The bottom player holds no matter what. If the top player breaks free and gets outside, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting past his legs and feet.

games.title: Introductory Pin Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest on top of him.
games.text: Top player: hold chest to chest and keep the bottom player there. Bottom player: push the top player off and get your legs back in front.

win.text: holds the pin.
wins by pushing the top player off and getting his legs back in front.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player pushes him off and gets his legs back, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding someone down, then escaping.

sessions.connection: Staying safe and guarded on the mat before you trust a partner is the same guard you use before you trust a room. Both are smart. Naming it is the work.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and a chest-to-chest pin. Staying guarded before you trust a partner is smart, the same way it is before you trust a room. You get to decide how much guard to keep, and when to drop it.

concept.lesson: Before you trust someone, you work from a grip you already have.
concept.question: Tonight you scored touches on his hands and knees. Where did each touch start?

options.text: From a grip you already had.
From a wild grab at anything.
options.feedback: Wild grabs leave you open.

options.text: From diving in close to him.
options.feedback: Diving in skips reading him first.

concept.bridge: Before you trust someone, you start small, from what you already have.

sessions.probingQuestion: Who are you when people are watching?

games.title: Hand Fight to Underhook Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, fully disconnected, hand fighting range.
games.text: Get one hand on each of two targets, wrist, elbow, or head, in any mix. Then fight to the underhook.

win.text: wins. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is a hand fight for the underhook.

games.title: Keep Feet Off — Belly Up Open Guard Introduction
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player starts with his hands on the bottom player, and may not go past the knees.
games.text: Bottom player: hook or post your feet on the top player any way you want, and use your hands too. Make him sit down, then get your own back off the mat. Top player: keep the bottom player on his back and your feet off his body, working step by step toward the knee pits, without going past the knees.

win.text: wins when the top player's butt hits the mat and then his own back comes off the mat.
wins by keeping the bottom player on his back for 30 seconds.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player sits him down and gets his own back up, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is keeping his feet off you.

games.title: Riding Bottom Position Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his hands and knees. The top player is on top with open hands around the bottom player's hips.
games.text: Top player: stay attached to the hips, break the bottom player down, and stop him from standing. Bottom player: build your base, fight to your feet, and turn to face the top player.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the bottom player flat on his side or belly.
wins by standing up and turning to face the top player.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player stands and turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is staying on top, hands and knees.

sessions.connection: Keeping your guard means keeping a boundary between you and the other person. The mask does the same job with people. Guard retention on the mat and the mask you wear are the same thing.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and riding position. Keeping your guard means keeping a boundary, and a mask does that same job with people. You get to choose what your mask protects, and naming it is the first step to owning it.

concept.lesson: Grip the wrists, elbows, and head on purpose, even with people watching.
concept.question: Tonight you hand fought for the underhook. What did your hands go for?

options.text: His wrists, elbows, and head, on purpose.
Whatever part of him was closest.
options.feedback: Closest is not the same as on purpose.

options.text: Nothing, until he grabbed you first.
options.feedback: Waiting gives him the first grip.

concept.bridge: Who you are when people watch shows in what you do on purpose.

sessions.probingQuestion: What version of you shows up here, and where did you learn it?

games.title: Uneven Hand Fight Game (Upper vs Lower)
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range. One is the underhook player, one is the leg player.
games.text: Underhook player: hand fight and get one underhook, staying upright. Leg player: hand fight and pick up one leg, connecting both hands around it anywhere from hip to ankle.

win.text: wins with one underhook.
wins by picking up the underhook player's leg.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting for an underhook or leg.

games.title: Open Guard Multiple Connection Game
games.start: The top player stands, fully connected. The bottom player has inside hooks and a knee-pit grip.
games.text: Bottom player: stay connected, or get the connection back if it slips. Use it to put the top player on his butt or hands, then stand up and make his back touch the mat. Top player: put the bottom player on his back and fight to the knee pit or the outside, staying on your feet.

win.text: wins by knocking the top player down and standing, or by sitting up to grab his legs or hips.
wins by touching his shin behind the bottom player's knee, or to his body from beside his legs.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is knocking a standing partner down.

games.title: Rear Hip Connection - Keep Belly Down (Turtle)
games.start: The defender is on his elbows and knees. The attacker is behind him with his hands locked around the defender's waist.
games.text: Attacker: keep the defender belly down, using knee-to-knee and foot-to-foot blocking to pull his hips to the mat. Defender: rise to a quad pod, both knees and both elbows off the floor.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the defender belly down.
wins by getting up on his hands and feet with his knees off the mat.

games.reset: The attacker holds no matter what. If the defender reaches a quad pod, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is keeping a balled up man flat.

sessions.connection: The guard you keep was drilled into you somewhere, and so was the mask. Both are learned defenses. Finding where you learned to guard is the same move on and off the mat.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and turtle. The guard you keep on the mat was learned somewhere, and so was your mask. Both were smart moves once, in the place you learned them. You get to keep what still helps you and set down what doesn't.

concept.lesson: Block his knees and feet with yours to keep him belly down.
concept.question: Tonight you kept a balled up partner belly down. What held him there?

options.text: Blocking his knees and feet with yours.
Lying on him with all your weight.
options.feedback: Weight alone lets him push up.

options.text: Squeezing his waist as hard as you can.
options.feedback: Squeezing tires you out before he does.

concept.bridge: The version of you that shows up here is the one you practice.

sessions.probingQuestion: What does your mask protect you from?

games.title: Consecutive Touches with Clinch Counter
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, no grips.
games.text: Touch player: collect three sets of two touches in a row. A touch is making the clinch player's hands touch the mat, or gripping behind one of his knees. Clinch player: close both hands around the touch player under both elbows or chest to back. Headlock, hips, or ankle clinches do not count.

win.text: wins with three sets of two touches in a row.
wins by closing his own hands around the touch player, under both elbows or chest to back.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is scoring quick touches before a hug.

games.title: Knee Pit Touchdown Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is standing and starts by clearing the feet.
games.text: Top player: clear the feet, then step one leg into one knee pit, then the other, in any order, keeping your feet off. Bottom player: hook and post with your feet, and use your hands to make him hit his butt, then sit up.

win.text: wins by touching the backs of both of the bottom player's knees with his shin, one and then the other.
wins by making the top player sit down, then sitting up himself.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting past his legs and feet.

games.title: Mount — Stay Under Both Elbows (Continuous)
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is in mount with both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
games.text: Top player: stay under at least one elbow the whole round. If you lose one, fight to get it back. Bottom player: get both elbows to touch your own body with nothing under them, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps an arm under one of the bottom player's elbows.
wins by touching both elbows to his body, or making the top player fall.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If he loses both elbows, that is the bottom player's win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is sitting on top of his belly.

sessions.connection: Your guard protects the space behind your legs. Your mask protects something too. Naming what the guard defends is the same as naming what the mask hides.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and mount. Your guard protects your legs, and your mask protects something in you. Naming what your mask guards is the same skill as naming what a guard defends. You get to use your mask on purpose.

concept.lesson: His legs guard the space in front of him. Your shin behind his knee gets you past.
concept.question: Tonight you got past his legs while he lay on his back. What got you in?

options.text: Your shin stepping behind his knee.
Jumping over both of his legs.
options.feedback: Jumping gives his feet a chance to push you.

options.text: Pulling his head toward you.
options.feedback: His head is not where the gap is.

concept.bridge: His legs protect his body, the way a mask protects what is under it.

sessions.probingQuestion: What happens to your mask when you're losing?

games.title: Single Leg — Make Partner Fall to Hands or Hips (Terminal)
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker is connected to one of the defender's legs.
games.text: Attacker: move the defender using only that leg, run him, pull him, turn him, or lift him, to make his hips or hands touch the mat. Defender: stay balanced and use your connections to break the grip and free your leg.

win.text: wins when the defender's hips or hands touch the mat.
wins by freeing his own leg from the attacker's grip.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is a takedown to one leg.

games.title: Closed Guard Opening — Hands on Body
games.start: The bottom player has closed guard locked around the top player. The top player is inside the guard, hands on him.
games.text: Top player: hold the bottom player down, get to your feet, and press on his hips, knees, and feet to open his legs. Bottom player: keep your legs closed, using only open-hand grips on the head, wrists, and elbows.

win.text: wins by standing up and opening the bottom player's legs so his ankles uncross.
wins by stopping the top player's win for 30 seconds. Then switch.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is standing to open his locked legs.

games.title: Referee Position Ride and Break Down
games.start: The bottom player is on his hands and knees. The top player is in referee position with open hands on his hips.
games.text: Top player: ride the bottom player, break him down, and keep his hips and hands on the mat, no closed-hand connections. Bottom player: build your base, fight to your feet, and turn to face.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the bottom player flat on his side or belly.
wins when he stands up and faces the top player.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player stands and faces him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is flattening someone on hands and knees.

sessions.connection: When your guard gets passed, the mask cracks and something real shows. Getting passed on the mat and cracking under pressure are the same moment. You feel it in your body first.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from a single leg, closed guard, and referee position. When your guard gets passed, something real slips out from under the mask. That crack is not failure, it is information. You get to notice what shows up and decide what to do with it.

concept.lesson: Keep him moving while you stay on the leg.
concept.question: Tonight you held one of his legs while he fought to get it back. What made him fall?

options.text: Keeping him moving while you held on.
Holding still and squeezing harder.
options.feedback: Holding still gives him time to free his leg.

options.text: Letting go to grab something else.
options.feedback: Letting go gives the leg back.

concept.bridge: When a round goes bad, keep moving. That is when the real you shows.

sessions.probingQuestion: What slips out of you when you get tired and stop performing?

games.title: Hand Fight with Leg Pickup Option
games.start: Both players stand and hand fight for wrist, elbow, and head connections.
games.text: Get an inside, outside, or under-elbow connection. Then pick up your partner's leg at the knee or ankle.

win.role: Whoever controls and picks up a leg first
win.text: wins. The same rule applies to both players.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting to pick up a leg.

games.title: Feet-Off Guard Passing Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is in front of him, hands already on him.
games.text: Top player: keep his feet off by clearing them and closing distance, stepping inside the knees or around the outside. Bottom player: use hooks, feet on the body, and posts to make the top player hit his butt or hands, then sit up with your back off the mat.

win.text: wins by pressing his shin on the bottom player's belly or side.
wins by making the top player fall on his butt, then getting his own back off the mat.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting past his legs and feet.

games.title: Pinning — Continuous Hip and Shoulder Connection from All Fours
games.start: The bottom player is on his hands and knees. The top player is behind him, hands locked around his waist.
games.text: Top player: use knee-to-knee and foot-to-foot blocking to pull his hips to the mat, switching between the hip grip and wrist grips to keep him belly down. Bottom player: get to a quad pod, both hands and both feet on the mat at the same time.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the bottom player belly down.
wins by getting up on his hands and feet with his knees off the mat.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player reaches a quad pod, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is keeping someone flat from behind.

sessions.connection: When you and your partner get tired, the fake stuff drops on both sides, the passer and the guard. What slips out when you are too tired to perform is the truest thing about you, on the mat and off.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and turtle. When you get tired, the performing stops, and something truer shows up in its place. That truer version is worth paying attention to, not hiding again. You get to decide what you do with what you noticed.

concept.lesson: Tired hands grab anything. Keep gripping wrists and elbows on purpose.
concept.question: Tonight the hand fight ran long and you got tired. What did your hands need to do?

options.text: Keep gripping wrists and elbows on purpose.
Grab anywhere just to hold on.
options.feedback: Grabbing anywhere is what tired hands do.

options.text: Drop down and rest for a second.
options.feedback: Resting in the middle gives him the leg.

concept.bridge: When you're tired, the real you shows in where your hands go.

sessions.probingQuestion: When you crack, what's the first thing that shows?

games.title: Single Leg Takedown Game
games.start: Both players stand. The attacker is connected to one of the defender's legs at the knee.
games.text: Attacker: move the defender and make him fall toward his hands or hips, running him, pulling him, turning him, or lifting him, using only that leg. Defender: stay balanced and use your connections to break the grip and free your leg.

win.text: wins when the defender touches the mat with his hips or hands.
wins by freeing his own leg from the attacker's grip.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is a takedown to one leg.

games.title: Knee Pit Touchdown Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is standing and starts by clearing the feet.
games.text: Top player: clear the feet, then step one leg into one knee pit, then the other, keeping your feet off. Bottom player: hook and post with your feet, using your hands to make him hit his butt, then sit up.

win.text: wins by touching the backs of both of the bottom player's knees with his shin, one and then the other.
wins by making the top player sit down, then sitting up himself.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting past his legs and feet.

games.title: Chest-to-Chest Elbow Control Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest on top, both arms under both of the bottom player's elbows.
games.text: Top player: stay under the bottom player's elbows, keeping them away from his body. Bottom player: get both elbows to touch your body, or make the top player fall over.

win.text: wins by keeping the bottom player's elbows away from his body the whole time.
wins by bringing both elbows to his body, or making the top player fall.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player gets both elbows to his body, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding someone down by his elbows.

sessions.connection: The checkpoint where a guard always breaks is a tell, and so is the first thing that shows when you crack. Finding the exact break point on the mat is the same skill as knowing your own tell.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from a single leg, open guard, and a chest-to-chest pin. Every guard has an exact point where it breaks, and so do you. Finding that point is the same skill as knowing the sign you give off, so you can catch yourself before it runs the show.

concept.lesson: Stay under at least one elbow. Notice when one cracks free and get it back.
concept.question: Tonight he fought to pull his elbows in under you. What kept him down?

options.text: Staying under at least one elbow.
Lying flat on him with all your weight.
options.feedback: Weight alone won't stop his elbows.

options.text: Letting go to grab his head.
options.feedback: Letting go frees both elbows.

concept.bridge: Noticing the first crack is how you stop it from growing.

sessions.probingQuestion: What's under the version you show people?

games.title: Waist-Centric Underhook Game
games.start: Both players stand. The underhook player has an underhook. The overhook player has an overhook.
games.text: Underhook player: move your partner and get to the head, waist, or a leg. The waist wins right away. A head or leg connection must be turned into a waist connection to win. Overhook player: use the overhook to keep him away, freeing the head or leg before he reaches the waist.

win.text: wins by locking his hands around the overhook player's waist.
wins by freeing his head or leg before the underhook player gets to his waist.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting an underhook to his waist.

games.title: Around-the-Legs Passing Game
games.start: The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is on his feet, starting by clearing the feet.
games.text: Top player: get one leg outside the bottom player's feet, make shin contact from knee to head, then without stopping go around to the other side and touch there too. Bottom player: hook and post with your feet to make the top player hit his butt, then sit up with your back off the mat.

win.text: wins by touching his shin to one side of the bottom player's body, then going around and touching the other side.
wins by making the top player fall on his butt, then getting his own back off the mat.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is getting around the legs.

games.title: Figure Four Grip Control Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player covers his head with a figure-four grip, one hand on the wrist, the other arm under the elbow.
games.text: Top player: keep the figure-four grip and stay under at least one elbow while keeping the bottom player pinned. Bottom player: break the grip by freeing your arms and getting your elbows to your body.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the grip.
wins by breaking the grip.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player breaks the grip, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding one arm with both hands.

sessions.connection: Getting past the legs shows what the guard was hiding. Looking under your mask shows the real you. Passing and revealing are the same move: get past the defense to what is behind it.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, open guard, and a figure-four pin. Getting past a guard shows what it was hiding, and looking under your mask works the same way. What is underneath is not worse, it is just true. You get to keep what is real.

concept.lesson: Clear his feet before anything else to get past the front.
concept.question: Tonight you got around his legs to his side. What did you clear first?

options.text: His feet, before anything else.
His head, so he couldn't see.
options.feedback: His feet stay in your way.

options.text: His arms, so he couldn't grab.
options.feedback: His feet can still push you off.

concept.bridge: To see what is under the front, you get past the first layer.

sessions.probingQuestion: What part of you have you been hiding, even from yourself?

games.title: Hand Fight with Precondition Game
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, not gripped, starting to hand fight.
games.text: Collect three touches. A touch is a hand behind your partner's knee or an underhook. Any mix counts. Only after three touches can you try for a closed-hand connection.

win.role: Whoever first gets three touches and then locks his hands around his partner
win.text: wins, anywhere from shoulders to ankles.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is fighting to wrap him up.

games.title: Side Half Guard — Clear Hands to Get Under Elbow
games.start: The bottom player is on his side in half guard, hands fully out on the top player. The top player is inside.
games.text: Top player: clear the bottom player's hands and get under one or both elbows, then connect your hands. Bottom player: keep your hands on the top player to deny that spot, and close your legs around his waist.

win.text: wins by locking his hands with an arm under one of the bottom player's elbows.
wins by closing his legs around the top player's waist.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is clearing his arms to get under.

games.title: Introductory Pin Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his back. The top player is chest to chest on top of him.
games.text: Top player: hold chest to chest and keep the bottom player there. Bottom player: push the top player off and get your legs back in front.

win.text: holds the pin.
wins by pushing the top player off and getting his legs back in front.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player pushes him off and gets his legs back, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is holding someone down, then escaping.

sessions.connection: Arriving past the guard puts you in touch with what was most protected. Naming the shadow does the same thing inside you. Both reach the thing that was hidden deepest.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, half guard, and a chest-to-chest pin. Arriving past a guard puts you in touch with what was most protected. Naming the part of yourself you keep hidden works the same way. You get to name it silently, for you, and that is brave.

concept.lesson: Earn three touches before you reach for the lock.
concept.question: Tonight you needed three touches before you could wrap him up. What let you wrap him?

options.text: Earning your three touches first.
Grabbing for the lock right away.
options.feedback: The lock only counts after three touches.

options.text: Waiting for him to hold still.
options.feedback: He won't hold still for you.

concept.bridge: What is hidden has to be earned, one touch at a time.

sessions.probingQuestion: If the mask came off in here, who would we meet?

games.title: Hand Touch / Knee Touch with Close Hand Connection
games.start: Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, in a neutral position. A knee grip must be behind the knee, not the front.
games.text: Win one of two ways: collect three touches in any mix (making your partner's hands touch the mat, or gripping behind one of his knees), or close both hands around his head, body, or leg. Take whichever one shows up.

win.text: wins, whether by three touches or by locking his hands around his partner's head, body, or leg.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is a standing game of touches.

games.title: Open Guard Takedown and Escape Game
games.start: The top player stands. The bottom player is on his back, fully connected, hands on the top player's ankles, feet inside his legs.
games.text: Bottom player: stay connected while putting the top player down on his hips or hands, then stand up, or stay connected as he rises. Top player: break the connections and make shin contact to pass.

win.text: wins by knocking the top player down and standing up, or by coming up while still holding on to him.
wins by going around the bottom player's legs and touching him with a shin.

games.reset: Win it and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run it again. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is knocking a man down, then standing.

games.title: Riding Bottom Position Game
games.start: The bottom player is on his hands and knees. The top player is on top with open hands around the bottom player's hips.
games.text: Top player: stay attached to the hips, break the bottom player down, and stop him from standing. Bottom player: build your base, fight to your feet, and turn to face the top player.

win.text: holds as long as he keeps the bottom player flat on his side or belly.
wins by standing up and turning to face the top player.

games.reset: The top player holds no matter what. If the bottom player stands and turns to face him, that is his win, and you start over. Roles switch after every win.
games.whatItIs: This is staying on top, hands and knees.

sessions.connection: Running both games from standing to a pin is the mat's version of the whole Descent, from arrival to the real self revealed. This session brings both journeys together into one.
sessions.takeaway: Tonight you worked from the hand fight, open guard, and riding position, standing to a pin in one round. That is the same trip you have made since Session 1. You showed up, you cracked, and you stayed anyway. You get to keep showing up as that person.

concept.lesson: Stay on your feet instead of dropping to your knees.
concept.question: Tonight he tried to knock you down from his back. What kept you up?

options.text: Staying on your feet, not your knees.
Dropping to your knees to rest.
options.feedback: On your knees, he can tip you over.

options.text: Leaning over to grab his head.
options.feedback: Leaning over gives him your balance.

concept.bridge: With the mask off, you still stay on your feet.
